Find the smallest natural number \( n \) for which the following condition is satisfied: if a number \( p \) is a prime and \( n \) is divisible by \( p-1 \) then \( n \) is divisible by \( p \).

***

We need the smallest natural number \( n \) such that for every prime \( p \) with \( (p-1) \mid n \) we also have \( p \mid n \).

***

First note that \( p-1=1 \) gives \( p=2 \) and since \( 1 \mid n \) always holds we must have \( 2 \mid n \). Then since \( 2 \mid n \) we get \( p-1=2 \) so \( p=3 \) must divide \( n \). Then since \( 6 \mid n \) we get \( p-1=6 \) so \( p=7 \) must divide \( n \).

***

Now \( 42 \mid n \) and \( p-1=42 \) gives \( p=43 \) which is prime so \( 43 \mid n \). This means \( 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 7 \cdot 43 = 1806 \mid n \).

***

We verify that \( n=1806=2 \cdot 3 \cdot 7 \cdot 43 \) satisfies the condition by checking every divisor \( d \) of \( 1806 \) to see if \( d+1 \) is prime. The divisors of \( 1806 \) are \( 1 \) and \( 2 \) and \( 3 \) and \( 6 \) and \( 7 \) and \( 14 \) and \( 21 \) and \( 42 \) and \( 43 \) and \( 86 \) and \( 129 \) and \( 258 \) and \( 301 \) and \( 602 \) and \( 903 \) and \( 1806 \).

***

Among these only \( d=1 \) giving \( p=2 \) and \( d=2 \) giving \( p=3 \) and \( d=6 \) giving \( p=7 \) and \( d=42 \) giving \( p=43 \) yield primes. All four of these primes divide \( 1806 \) so the condition is fully satisfied.

***

Since \( n \) must be divisible by \( 2 \) and \( 3 \) and \( 7 \) and \( 43 \) the smallest possible value is their product which is \( \boxed{1806} \).
